narration_use: reference only when drafting; required units must be derivable from the public B2 inputs (table + intent)
file_naming: one G1 per input contract; B1/B3/B4/B5 need separate drafts
intent: To demonstrate that a majority of U.S. adults expressed at least some confidence in police officers to act in the public's best interests in late 2020.

units.meaning: Combining the two reported confidence levels, 74% of U.S. adults expressed at least some confidence in police to act in the public's best interests.
accepted_routes: about three-quarters said a great deal or a fair amount
26% great deal plus 48% fair amount equals 74% at least some confidence
units.visual_evidence_rule: The chart must show both the 26% and 48% components or a combined 74% 'at least some' segment.
units.temporal_anchor: the narration clause 'most said they have at least some confidence'
units.reviewer_question: Is the combined 74% at-least-some figure obligatory even though it is derived rather than printed?

units.meaning: 26% of U.S. adults said they had a great deal of confidence in police to act in the public's best interests.
accepted_routes: about one-quarter reported a great deal of confidence
units.visual_evidence_rule: The 'A great deal' bar/segment must be labeled or readable as 26%.
units.temporal_anchor: the clause 'with 26 % saying they have a great deal'
units.reviewer_question: Must the exact 26% great-deal value be shown?

units.meaning: 48% of U.S. adults said they had a fair amount of confidence in police to act in the public's best interests.
accepted_routes: about half reported a fair amount of confidence
units.visual_evidence_rule: The 'A fair amount' bar/segment must be labeled or readable as 48%.
units.temporal_anchor: the narration clause 'most said they have at least some confidence' or the supporting data reveal
units.reviewer_question: Must the exact 48% fair-amount value be shown even though the narration does not name it?

units.meaning: The 'fair amount' share was 22 percentage points larger than the 'great deal' share (48% vs. 26%).
accepted_routes: fair amount was 22 points higher than great deal
great deal was 22 percentage points lower than fair amount
units.visual_evidence_rule: Both bars or segments must be visible so the 22-point gap can be inferred or labeled.
units.temporal_anchor: the clause contrasting 'at least some confidence' with '26% saying they have a great deal'
units.reviewer_question: Should the video explicitly state the 22-point gap, or is showing both bars enough?

units.meaning: The combined at-least-some share (74%) is more than half, so it represents a majority of U.S. adults.
accepted_routes: more than half had at least some confidence
the majority said they had at least some confidence
units.visual_evidence_rule: The chart must show the combined 74% or the two components summing past the halfway point.
units.temporal_anchor: the clause 'most said they have at least some confidence'
units.reviewer_question: Is the majority interpretation of the 74% figure required separately from the 74% share itself?

optional_valid: A fair amount was the most common of the two shown confidence levels (48%).
The great-deal share (26%) is about one-quarter of adults.
The fair-amount share (48%) is roughly half of adults.
unsupported_to_avoid: Causal claims about why confidence was high or low or how policing experiences affected it.
Breakdowns by political or demographic groups not present in the table.
Any third confidence category such as 'not much' or 'none at all' values not in the table.
Using relative_value 0.2573 + 0.4750 = 0.7323 as the at-least-some share if it contradicts the printed 26% + 48% = 74% route.
notes: The key required content is the 74% at-least-some composition and its majority interpretation, with 26% and 48% as components; the 22-point gap and ranking are optional trade-offs. Keep the video focused on these reported confidence levels and avoid unsupported external breakdowns or causes.
weight_mode_note: every unit gets 1/n so coverage is a plain share; weight_template is kept for per-type analysis only
